title: Armstrong gave Red Allen an hour of his own
summary: Armstrong let Red Allen's own book fill an hour, then returned with one note that brought the house down.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Because Henry Allen was in that band, and you mentioned earlier how he didn't hold Henry Allen back at all.

Yeah, Louis was not the type to hold anybody back. If you could do anything, he'd let you do it, and he'd be glad to promote you. In fact, he wanted that very much. Do something, do it, and do it good. Just like with Red Allen... Red Allen was a great trumpet player in the band, and a lot of people actually thought Red was better than Louis was -- Red had his following, too. But Louis gave Red an hour's time on his own, to play his own numbers; and anything he wanted to do, he would give Red an hour to do it. And Louis would get off the scene. He wouldn't even be seen on the stage. So Red could do anything he wanted to play, and he did it, too.
Red had his own book of numbers.
Red had his own library, books and numbers

and everything else. He played nothing but Red Allen's numbers. And he did all right. But now, when it's time for Louis to come back, Louis would come walking on across the stage, and he'd take his horn and play one note on the horn -- and brother, it sounded like the roof fell in or somethin'. They'd be whoopin' and hollerin', and poor Red, he was forgotten about right away. He was forgotten about right away.

But I mean, Louis was that type of person. He didn't stop nobody. He'd give them a whole hour. And that's very unusual for somebody working with a man like Louis or anybody else, and somebody else playing the same instrument, too -- you wouldn't give them no hour. He'd give him the whole hour, and let him prove himself. Well, then, all Louis would do was come back and hit one note. And it was all the difference in the world! All the difference in the world
